Teamcenter\-X Procedures

# <a id="_Toc137691973"></a>Change Management

##### Purpose of this document is to describe Change Management Procedure for Teamcenter X\.

##### Policy Tag

##### [Siemens Industry Software \(SISW\) SaaS Change Management Policy\.pdf](https://siemensnam.sharepoint.com/:b:/r/teams/disw_ISMS/Policies/Siemens%20Industry%20Software%20(SISW)%20SaaS%20Change%20Management%20Policy.pdf?csf=1&web=1&e=wxpcpD) 

##### Scope

The document address changes arriving TeamcenterX from various sources including:

1. Issues filed by customers\.
2. Security vulnerabilities identified by Black Duck and Security Pentest or TRA process
3. Teamcenter patches
4. Teamcenter X Addons

All these requests are recorded in MyPolarion as features, defects, or security issues\. They are tracked by Release Management team for closure\.

## <a id="_Toc137691974"></a>Sources of changes

Changes to Teamcenter product or the development environment can come from 3 different sources\. 

### Changes to TeamcenterX product

This includes changes to due to Customer requests, addons, security issues and updates to Teamcenter\.

### Changes to Development Systems

This includes changes to the development infrastructure due to Patching of OS/EC2/ECRs, Security Patching, and mitigating a vulnerability\.

### Changes to 3rd party components in TeamcenterX

The 3rd party components used in TeamcenterX Kit may need to be changes due to security issues, bugs or version upgrades\.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Figure 1: Sources of change

### Procedure for creating a change request

TeamcenterX following the Change Management Control Procedure established for the LCS\. Change requests are management in Mypolarian\. The details for creating a change request and control are available as [Working Agreement \- Change Management Control\.](https://mypolarion.industrysoftware.automation.siemens.com/polarion/#/project/PL/wiki/Working_Agreements/Working%20Agreement%20-%20Change%20Management%20Control)

## <a id="_Toc133323327"></a><a id="_Toc133323547"></a><a id="_Toc137691976"></a><a id="_Toc137691977"></a>Procedure for managing the change

### Procedure for changes originating from customer issues

1. Issues identified by customers are assigned to Teamcenter X team through Incident Requests \(IR\)\. 
2. The team triages the defects and assigns them to respective teams by creating a Defect/Problem Report \(PR\) or Enhancement Request \(ER\)\. 
3. The defects can be assigned and processed to either of the following based on the type of change\.
	1. Teamcenter core team, 
	2. Add On Solutions team,
	3. Teamcenter X team\.

### Procedure for security related changes originating internally or externally

Security Issues are items identified by LCS security team and assigned for processing\. These may originate from e\.g\., penetration tests, automated scanning, vulnerability monitoring or risk assessments\. [Working Agreement on Security Issues](https://mypolarion.industrysoftware.automation.siemens.com/polarion/#/project/PL/wiki/Working_Agreements/Working%20Agreement%20-%20Security%20Issue%20Workitem) describes the process for handling security issues\.

Security Defects are items originating from customers via PR’s\. The [Working Agreement \- Security Defects \(External\)](https://mypolarion.industrysoftware.automation.siemens.com/polarion/#/project/Teamcenter/wiki/Working%20Agreements%20-%20AW/workingAgreementSLA) describes the process for handling security defects\.

### Procedure for changes originating from Teamcenter regular updates

Teamcenter Release Management follows a patch release cadence which will be evaluated and applied to customer deployments\. [Working Agreement \- Patch Management](https://mypolarion.industrysoftware.automation.siemens.com/polarion/#/project/Teamcenter/wiki/Working%20Agreements%20-%20AW/Working%20Agreement%20-%20Patch%20Management) explains in detail the process of Teamcenter Patch Management\.

### Procedure for changes originating from Addons to TeamcenterX

TcX is an aggregated solution involving code changes of Teamcenter, Addon Solutions and Infrastructure orchestration scripts\. TcX Addons change management generally follows Teamcenter processes and are the responsibility of the Addon team\. TcX Addons may trigger changes in TcX itself as follows:

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Figure 3: Changes due to Addons

## <a id="_Toc137691979"></a>Procedure for Vulnerability Management

Vulnerabilities in the TcX development environment are available at the [Security Hub Dashboard\.](https://splunk.sws.siemens.com/en-US/app/securityhub/securityhub__inspector__v2?form.finding_token=*&form.account_token=*&form.saas_token=*&form.region_token=*&form.compliance_token=*&form.scan_token=AWS_EC2_INSTANCE&form.vuln_token=No&form.severity_token=CRITICAL&form.severity_token=HIGH&form.name_token=*&form.id_token=*&form.raw_token=No&form.dedup_token=No&form.ldap_token=*&form.group_token=TcX)

3 different types of vulnerabilities are monitored by CSO and are available at this dashboard\.

1. EC2
2. ECR
3. Lambda 

Scrums are responsible to monitor the security hub dashboard periodically to check vulnerabilities in the team specific instances\. The workflow after this is as below:

 

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Figure 5: Vulnerability management workflow

### Workflow

1.  The scrums or a nominated team member as security responsible for each team is required to monitor the security hub at least once in a week\.
2. Security responsible would triage the vulnerabilities and based on the risk and severity shall prioritize patching\.
3. The fix shall be assigned to team members who are managing the instance of the account e\.g lambda, EC2 or ECRs\.
4. The instances are tested after the fix for bugs\.
5. The Security responsible shall verify that the fix is working, and the vulnerability is fixed by checking the security hub again\. *\(Note: the security hub may take few hours to update\)*
6. The learnings like the configuration issues or root cause of the vulnerability shall be documented\. This would help the security responsible to minimize the security issue reoccurrence\.

## <a id="_Toc137691980"></a>Procedure for system patching of dev accounts\.

The system patches include patching the security issues in AWS development environment\. 

![A picture containing font, circle, logo, line

Description automatically generated](data:image/png;base64,)

Figure 6: Workflow for AWS System patching

### Procedure to Create IAM Patch Manager

To set\-up IAM roles for accessing patch manager from master account following steps needs to be executed by AWS account owners on their respective AWS accounts\. 

1. Ensure that AWS cli installed and configured on workstation\. 
2. Create required roles and permissions in DEV accounts: 
3. Team Bastion has created a shell script which will create required roles and permissions\. 
4. Open the git bash, configure aws cli for the specific account and run below command to download shell script from a s3 bucket: “aws s3 cp s3://tcx\-os\-patching\-automation/OSPatch\-TargetAccountRoles\.sh”\. 
5. After downloading OSPatch\-TargetAccountRoles\.sh file, at the same location run below command  

 			\./OSPatch\-TargetAccountRoles\.sh 

 This will create required roles and permissions in your account\.

### Procedure to schedule a patching plan

Ansible tower jobs are used to schedule the patching\. To have minimal disruption to regular work the patching is scheduled on every __Saturday\.__ this job will do as below \-

1. It will start all the instances in respective dev accounts 
2. If anyone want to exclude specific instances during patching, then they can add a tag with “key:NO\_PATCH value:true” before patching\.
3. For windows instances, it will create custom security group which will open ports 80, 443, and 49152 \- 65535 which are required for patching\.
4. It will create custom patch baselines for WINDOWS and RHEL instances as per the requirement\.
5. After completing all the above process, it will start patching process for all running instances\.
6. Once patching is done, it will remove custom attached security group from windows instances\.

### Procedure to check patching status

To check the patching status from target account, follow the below process\.

1. Open AWS Systems Manager console\.
2. Go to Node management and click on Patch Manager\.
3. In Non\-patch policy\-based operations, Information about recent patching operations can be seen, including details like how the operation was initiated, when it was completed, and whether it was successful\.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Figure 7: System patching status

Patching status and the reason could be following:

Status

Reason

Time\-out

Specific instance is not in running condition\.

Success

Patching is successful on that specific instance

Failed

Patching is failed because of some error\.

![A screenshot of a computer

Description automatically generated with medium confidence](data:image/png;base64,)

Figure 8: Status of executed steps

1. If the status is failed, the details of the error can be seen by clicking on the operation and then clicking on the Instance Id\.
2. In case of Success details of applied patch can be seen following the steps below:
3. Go to __Node management__ and click on __Fleet Manager\.__
4. Select the Node \(Instance\) and click on __Patch__ option\.
5. In the patch Summary check patching time, how many updates installed, which patches are applied, etc\.

### Procedure to verify Vulnerabilities status after patching

After patching, OS related vulnerabilities will be reduced\. You can check the Vulnerabilities status either from AWS Inspector or from [Splunk](https://splunk.sws.siemens.com/en-US/app/securityhub/securityhub__inspector__v2) dashboard\.

![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

Figure 9: Splunk dashboard for vulnerability status
